title: Countable specialization antichain with the same closure
statement: Let $U$ be a Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme], meaning a quasi-compact locally Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth, def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. For every subset $E\subseteq|U|$ there is an at most countable subset $D\subseteq E$ with $\overline D=\overline E$ and with no specialization between distinct elements: if $v,w\in D$ and $w\in\overline{\{v\}}$, then $v=w$. Closures are taken in the underlying topological space of $U$. The empty and finite cases are included.

source.place: Tags 0G2F (lemma-countable-dense-subset), applied on the reduced closed subscheme with space the closure of E, and 0G2R (lemma-maximal-points), applied to the resulting countable subset; finite cases included.

proof.text: Write $Z_x=\overline{\{x\}}$ for $x\in |U|$, and define $Q$ to be the set of $x$ for which there exists an at most countable $C_x\subseteq E\cap Z_x$ with $\overline{C_x}=Z_x$. Choose one such witness for each $x\in Q$. For $x\in E$ the witness $\{x\}$ works, so $E\subseteq Q$. For every $x\in Q$, the equality $Z_x=\overline{C_x}$ gives $x\in\overline E$. Thus $E\subseteq Q\subseteq\overline E$, including when $E$ is empty.

source.place: Tag 0G2F, lemma-countable-dense-subset, first paragraph: the set T' and its witnesses E_s

proof.text: For any at most countable $A\subseteq Q$, put $C=\bigcup_{x\in A} C_x$. A countable union of at most countable sets is at most countable, and $C\subseteq E$. Each $x\in A$ belongs to $\overline{C_x}\subseteq\overline C$, while $C_x\subseteq Z_x\subseteq\overline A$ for $x\in A$. Taking closures proves $\overline C=\overline A$. This also holds for $A=\varnothing$.

source.place: Tag 0G2F, lemma-countable-dense-subset, first paragraph: closure of E' equals closure of the union of E_s

proof.text: For $A$ and $C$ as in step 2, decompose the closed set $F=\overline A=\overline C$ into its finitely many distinct irreducible components $Z_1,\ldots,Z_r$ by [lem-sc-noetherian-closed-subset-finite-components]. Each $Z_i$, being closed in the closed set $F$, is closed in $U$, so [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-sober] supplies its generic point $\eta_i$. We claim $\overline{C\cap Z_i}=Z_i$. Indeed put $H_i=\bigcup_{j\ne i}Z_j$. Maximality and irreducibility imply $Z_i\not\subseteq H_i$: otherwise its finite closed cover by $Z_i\cap Z_j$ would force containment in a distinct component. Hence $O_i=F\setminus H_i$ is a nonempty open subset of $F$ contained in $Z_i$. Every nonempty open subset of the irreducible space $Z_i$ meets $O_i$, since two disjoint nonempty opens would give a cover by two proper closed subsets. Its intersection with $O_i$ is open in $F$ and therefore meets $C$, which is dense in $F$. Thus $C\cap Z_i$ is dense in $Z_i$. It is at most countable and lies in $E\cap Z_i$, so it witnesses $\eta_i\in Q$.

source.place: Tag 0G2F, lemma-countable-dense-subset, first paragraph: generic points of the components of the closure of E' belong to T'; the restriction-to-component density argument is written out

proof.text: Let $M=\{m\in Q:\text{ if }s\in Q\text{ and }m\in Z_s,\text{ then }s=m\}$. By [lem-sfb-subset-maximal-generalization] applied to $T=Q$, every point of $Q$ is in $Z_m$ for some $m\in M$. Suppose $M$ were infinite and choose a countably infinite subset $A\subseteq M$. Steps 2 and 3 apply to this $A$: the closed set $\overline A$ has finitely many components, with generic points $\eta_1,\ldots,\eta_r$ belonging to $Q$. For $a\in A$, some component $Z_i=\overline{\{\eta_i\}}$ contains $a$. Because $a\in M$ and $\eta_i\in Q$, the defining implication for $M$ gives $a=\eta_i$. Therefore $A\subseteq\{\eta_1,\ldots,\eta_r\}$, a contradiction. Consequently $M$ is finite.

source.place: Tag 0G2F, lemma-countable-dense-subset, second paragraph; Tag 0G2R, lemma-maximal-points, assertion (b) applied to T'

proof.text: Put $C=\bigcup_{m\in M} C_m$. It is at most countable and contained in $E$. The covering conclusion for $Q$ in step 4 gives $E\subseteq Q\subseteq\bigcup_{m\in M}Z_m$. For each $m\in M$, $Z_m=\overline{C_m}\subseteq\overline C$. Thus $E\subseteq\overline C$. Together with $C\subseteq E$ this gives $\overline C=\overline E$. If $M$ is empty, the same inclusions force $E=C=\varnothing$.

source.place: Tag 0G2F, lemma-countable-dense-subset, final sentence; this direct-in-U proof avoids introducing a reduced closed subscheme

proof.text: Finally define $D=\{d\in C:\text{ if }s\in C\text{ and }d\in Z_s,\text{ then }s=d\}$. It is a subset of the at most countable set $C$, hence is at most countable and lies in $E$. Apply [lem-sfb-subset-maximal-generalization] to $T=C$: for every $c\in C$ there is $d\in D$ with $c\in Z_d$. It follows that $C\subseteq\overline D$, whence $\overline C\subseteq\overline D$; the reverse inclusion follows from $D\subseteq C$. Consequently $\overline D=\overline E$. If $v,w\in D$ and $w\in Z_v$, then $v\in C$ and the defining implication for $w\in D$ gives $v=w$. All the constructions allow empty sets and finite sets, so no exceptional case is excluded.

lean.statement: theorem exists_countable_subset_closure_eq_no_specializations (U : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.{u}) [AlgebraicGeometry.IsLocallyNoetherian U] [CompactSpace U] (E : Set U) : ∃ D : Set U, D ⊆ E ∧ D.Countable ∧ closure D = closure E ∧ ∀ (v : U), v ∈ D → ∀ (w : U), w ∈ D → w ∈ closure ({v} : Set U) → v = w
